A Tier-B telemetry rebuild\n/// must observe the process environment at rebuild time, while a failed\n/// resolution leaves the caller's existing exporter candidate untouched.\nfn resolve_headers(headers: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {\n    headers\n        .iter()\n        .map(|header| {\n            let (key, raw_value) = header\n                .split_once(':')\n                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!(\"invalid OTLP header; expected 'name: value'\"))?;\n            let key = key.trim();\n            let raw_value = raw_value.trim();\n            if key.is_empty() || raw_value.is_empty() {\n                anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP header; name and value must be non-empty\");\n            }\n\n            let value = if let Some(variable) = raw_value.strip_prefix(\"env:\") {\n                if variable.is_empty() {\n                    anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP header environment reference\");\n                }\n                // Do not include the variable name or resolved value in the\n                // error. The caller may forward this diagnostic to a log or a\n                // reload event, and header material must never appear there.\n                std::env::var(variable).map_err(|_| {\n                    anyhow::anyhow!(\"OTLP header references an unavailable environment variable\")\n                })?\n            } else {\n                raw_value.to_string()\n            };\n            Ok((key.to_string(), value))\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Return the repository name used in browser-visible OTLP attributes.\n///\n/// Workspace paths are useful locally but are machine-specific and can expose\n/// filesystem details in the dashboard. drop_tx.send(DropEvent {\n                            signal: SignalType::Logs,\n                            dropped_count: 1,\n                        });\n                        failure_tracker.reset();\n                    }\n\n                    Err(e)\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// OTLP sink implementing the telemetry Sink trait.\n///\n/// Wraps the OpenTelemetry SDK providers and translates TelemetryEvent\n/// into traces, metrics, and logs per the semantic mapping.\n///\n/// ## Resilience\n///\n/// The OTel SDK's batch processors provide bounded queues that drop\n/// oldest items when full. Export failures are logged at WARN level\n/// but do not crash the worker. Shutdown has a 5-second timeout.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct OtlpSink {\n    /// Tracer provider for trace export.\n    tracer_provider: Arc<SdkTracerProvider>,\n    /// Meter provider for metric export.\n    meter_provider: Arc<SdkMeterProvider>,\n    /// Logger provider for log export.\n    logger_provider: Arc<SdkLoggerProvider>,\n    /// Cached metric instruments.\n    metrics: Metrics,\n    /// File sink for emitting drop events (never to OTLP, to avoid recursion).\n    /// Wrapped in Arc so it can be shared with the drop monitor task.\n    file_sink: Option<Arc<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>>,\n    /// Worker ID for drop events.\n    worker_id: String,\n    /// Session ID for drop events.\n    session_id: String,\n    /// Next sequence number for drop events.\n    next_drop_sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n    /// Observable state for gauges (heartbeat.age, queue.depth).\n    observable_state: Arc<ObservableState>,\n    /// Drop monitor task handle - kept alive to ensure the task runs.\n    _drop_monitor_handle: Arc<DropMonitorHandle>,\n}\n\n/// Handle to keep the drop monitor task alive.\n///\n/// Uses an atomic flag to signal shutdown to the monitor task.\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nstruct DropMonitorHandle {\n    shutdown: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n}\n\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nimpl DropMonitorHandle {\n    fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            shutdown: Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn is_shutdown(&self) -> bool {\n        self.shutdown.load(Ordering::Relaxed) != 0\n    }\n\n    fn shutdown(&self) {\n        self.shutdown.store(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Sequence number atomic for drop events.\n#[derive(Clone)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nstruct DropSequence(Arc<AtomicU64>);\n\n/// State for observable gauges.\n#[derive(Default)]\nstruct ObservableState {\n    /// Last heartbeat timestamp (UNIX epoch seconds).\n    last_heartbeat_secs: AtomicU64,\n    /// Queue depth per priority level (sampled at strand evaluation).\n    /// Maps priority -> count.\n    queue_depth_by_priority: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<u8, AtomicU64>>>,\n}\n\n/// Cached metric instruments for efficient recording.\n#[derive(Clone)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\nstruct Metrics {\n    /// UpDownCounter: `needle.workers.active`\n    workers_active: UpDownCounter<i64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.beads.claimed`\n    beads_claimed: Counter<u64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.beads.completed`\n    beads_completed: Counter<u64>,\n    /// Histogram: `needle.beads.duration`\n    bead_duration: Histogram<f64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.claim.attempts`\n    claim_attempts: Counter<u64>,\n    /// Histogram: `needle.strand.duration`\n    strand_duration: Histogram<f64>,\n    /// Histogram: `needle.agent.duration`\n    agent_duration: Histogram<f64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.agent.tokens.input`\n    tokens_input: Counter<u64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.agent.tokens.output`\n    tokens_output: Counter<u64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.cost.usd`\n    cost_usd: Counter<f64>,\n    /// ObservableGauge: `needle.heartbeat.age`\n    heartbeat_age: ObservableGauge<u64>,\n    /// ObservableGauge: `needle.queue.depth`\n    queue_depth: ObservableGauge<u64>,\n    /// UpDownCounter: `needle.peers.stale`\n    peers_stale: UpDownCounter<i64>,\n    /// Counter: `needle.mitosis.children_created`\n    mitosis_children_created: Counter<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl OtlpSink {\n    /// Create a new OTLP sink from configuration.\n    ///\n    /// Initializes the OpenTelemetry SDK with batch processors for\n    /// non-blocking export of all three signals.\n    ///\n    /// The `file_sink` parameter is used to emit shutdown timeout events\n    /// when the flush takes longer than 5 seconds.\n    ///\n    /// This constructs an independent candidate. Callers performing a live\n    /// rebuild must retain the current sink until this returns successfully;\n    /// header resolution happens during candidate construction and never\n    /// mutates the already-running exporter.\n    ///\n    /// The `agent`, `model`, `provider`, and `workspace` parameters are optional resource\n    /// attributes for OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.\n    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\n    pub fn new(\n        worker_id: String,\n        session_id: String,\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        file_sink: Option<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>,\n        agent: Option<&str>,\n        model: Option<&str>,\n        provider: Option<&str>,\n        workspace: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        // Build resource attributes from config + computed attributes\n        let resource = Self::build_resource(\n            &worker_id,\n            &session_id,\n            config,\n            agent,\n            model,\n            provider,\n            workspace,\n        )?;\n\n        // Create drop sequence atomic and monitor channel\n        let next_drop_sequence = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));\n        let (drop_tx, drop_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<DropEvent>();\n\n        // Wrap file_sink in Arc so it can be shared with drop monitor task\n        let file_sink_arc = file_sink.map(Arc::new);\n\n        // Drop monitor task spawn deferred to avoid runtime initialization issues\n        // The drop channel is created but the monitor task is not spawned during init\n        let _file_sink_for_monitor = file_sink_arc.clone();\n        let _worker_id_clone = worker_id.clone();\n        let _session_id_clone = session_id.clone();\n        let _next_drop_seq_clone = next_drop_sequence.clone();\n        let _drop_rx = drop_rx;\n        // Note: The drop monitor task would be spawned later in the worker's main runtime\n\n        // Build exporters based on protocol\n        let (tracer_provider, meter_provider, logger_provider) = match config.protocol.as_str() {\n            \"grpc\" => Self::build_grpc_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,\n            \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => Self::build_http_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,\n            other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n        };\n\n        // Build metric instruments\n        let meter = meter_provider.meter(\"needle\");\n        let observable_state = Arc::new(ObservableState::default());\n\n        // Clone Arc for each callback (they need to outlive this function)\n        let heartbeat_state = observable_state.clone();\n        let worker_id_for_callback = worker_id.clone();\n\n        // Register observable gauges with callbacks\n        let heartbeat_age = meter\n            .u64_observable_gauge(\"needle.heartbeat.age\")\n            .with_unit(\"s\")\n            .with_description(\"Seconds since last heartbeat emitted by this worker\")\n            .with_callback(move |observer| {\n                let now = SystemTime::now()\n                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n                    .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n                    .unwrap_or(0);\n                let last = heartbeat_state.last_heartbeat_secs.load(Ordering::Relaxed);\n                if last > 0 && now > last {\n                    observer.observe(\n                        now - last,\n                        &[KeyValue::new(\"worker_id\", worker_id_for_callback.clone())],\n                    );\n                }\n            })\n            .build();\n\n        // Clone Arc for queue depth callback\n        let queue_state = observable_state.clone();\n        // Capture workspace for queue depth attribute (bounded cardinality: one per worker)\n        let workspace_attr = workspace.map(workspace_label);\n\n        let queue_depth = meter\n            .u64_observable_gauge(\"needle.queue.depth\")\n            .with_unit(\"{bead}\")\n            .with_description(\"Open beads visible to this worker (sampled at strand evaluation)\")\n            .with_callback(move |observer| {\n                // Observe queue depth for each priority level\n                let guard = queue_state.queue_depth_by_priority.lock().unwrap();\n                for (priority, count) in guard.iter() {\n                    // Build attributes vector with priority and optional workspace\n                    let mut attrs = vec![KeyValue::new(\"priority\", i64::from(*priority))];\n                    if let Some(ref ws) = workspace_attr {\n                        attrs.push(KeyValue::new(\"workspace\", ws.clone()));\n                    }\n                    observer.observe(count.load(Ordering::Relaxed), &attrs);\n                }\n            })\n            .build();\n\n        let metrics = Metrics {\n            workers_active: meter\n                .i64_up_down_counter(\"needle.workers.active\")\n                .with_unit(\"{worker}\")\n                .with_description(\"Current live worker count\")\n                .build(),\n            beads_claimed: meter\n                .u64_counter(\"needle.beads.claimed\")\n                .with_unit(\"{bead}\")\n                .with_description(\"Successful bead claims\")\n                .build(),\n            beads_completed: meter\n                .u64_counter(\"needle.beads.completed\")\n                .with_unit(\"{bead}\")\n                .with_description(\"Bead terminal outcomes (one per bead.outcome)\")\n                .build(),\n            bead_duration: meter\n                .f64_histogram(\"needle.beads.duration\")\n                .with_unit(\"ms\")\n                .with_description(\"End-to-end bead lifecycle time\")\n                .build(),\n            claim_attempts: meter\n                .u64_counter(\"needle.claim.attempts\")\n                .with_unit(\"{attempt}\")\n                .with_description(\"Claim attempts\")\n                .build(),\n            strand_duration: meter\n                .f64_histogram(\"needle.strand.duration\")\n                .with_unit(\"ms\")\n                .with_description(\"Strand evaluation time\")\n                .build(),\n            agent_duration: meter\n                .f64_histogram(\"needle.agent.duration\")\n                .with_unit(\"ms\")\n                .with_description(\"Agent process runtime\")\n                .build(),\n            tokens_input: meter\n                .u64_counter(\"needle.agent.tokens.input\")\n                .with_unit(\"{token}\")\n                .with_description(\"Input tokens consumed\")\n                .build(),\n            tokens_output: meter\n                .u64_counter(\"needle.agent.tokens.output\")\n                .with_unit(\"{token}\")\n                .with_description(\"Output tokens produced\")\n                .build(),\n            cost_usd: meter\n                .f64_counter(\"needle.cost.usd\")\n                .with_unit(\"USD\")\n                .with_description(\"Estimated cost accumulator\")\n                .build(),\n            heartbeat_age,\n            queue_depth,\n            peers_stale: meter\n                .i64_up_down_counter(\"needle.peers.stale\")\n                .with_unit(\"{peer}\")\n                .with_description(\"Currently-stale peers observed by this worker\")\n                .build(),\n            mitosis_children_created: meter\n                .u64_counter(\"needle.mitosis.children_created\")\n                .with_unit(\"{bead}\")\n                .with_description(\"Mitosis child creations\")\n                .build(),\n        };\n\n        let drop_monitor_handle = Arc::new(DropMonitorHandle::new());\n\n        Ok(OtlpSink {\n            tracer_provider: Arc::new(tracer_provider),\n            meter_provider: Arc::new(meter_provider),\n            logger_provider: Arc::new(logger_provider),\n            metrics,\n            file_sink: file_sink_arc,\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            next_drop_sequence,\n            observable_state,\n            _drop_monitor_handle: drop_monitor_handle,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Background task that monitors for export failures and emits drop events.\n    ///\n    /// This task runs for the lifetime of the OtlpSink, receiving drop notifications\n    /// from exporter wrappers and emitting `telemetry.otlp.dropped` events to the\n    /// file sink only (never to OTLP, to avoid recursion).\n    #[allow(dead_code)] // Used in tests only\n    async fn drop_monitor_task(\n        mut drop_rx: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<DropEvent>,\n        file_sink: Option<Arc<Box<dyn crate::telemetry::Sink>>>,\n        worker_id: String,\n        session_id: String,\n        next_drop_sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,\n    ) {\n        while let Some(drop) = drop_rx.recv().await {\n            if let Some(sink) = &file_sink {\n                let sequence = next_drop_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n\n                let mut data = serde_json::map::Map::new();\n                data.insert(\n                    \"signal\".to_string(),\n                    serde_json::json!(drop.signal.as_str()),\n                );\n                data.insert(\n                    \"dropped_count\".to_string(),\n                    serde_json::json!(drop.dropped_count),\n                );\n                data.insert(\"queue_full\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));\n\n                let event = TelemetryEvent {\n                    timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),\n                    event_type: \"telemetry.otlp.dropped\".to_string(),\n                    worker_id: worker_id.clone(),\n                    session_id: session_id.clone(),\n                    sequence,\n                    bead_id: None,\n                    workspace: None,\n                    duration_ms: None,\n                    data: serde_json::Value::Object(data),\n                    trace_id: None,\n                    span_id: None,\n                };\n\n                // Emit to file sink - ignore errors to avoid recursion\n                let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n                    if let Err(e) = (**sink).accept(&event) {\n                        warn!(\"failed to write OTLP drop event to file sink: {e}\");\n                    }\n                }));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Build the OTel Resource with config and computed attributes.\n    ///\n    /// Merges three layers (lowest → highest precedence):\n    /// 1. OTel defaults (service.name = \"needle\", schema url)\n    /// 2. Computed attributes (set by NEEDLE at runtime)\n    /// 3. Config attributes (from telemetry.otlp.resource_attributes)\n    ///\n    /// Reserved keys `service.name` and `service.instance.id` cannot be overridden\n    /// via config - attempting to do so will return an error.\n    pub fn build_resource(\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        agent: Option<&str>,\n        model: Option<&str>,\n        provider: Option<&str>,\n        workspace: Option<&str>,\n    ) -> Result<Resource> {\n        // Reserved keys that cannot be overridden via config\n        const RESERVED_KEYS: &[&str] = &[\"service.name\", \"service.instance.id\"];\n\n        let mut builder = Resource::builder().with_attributes([\n            KeyValue::new(\"service.name\", \"needle\"),\n            KeyValue::new(\"service.namespace\", config.service_namespace.clone()),\n            KeyValue::new(\"service.version\", env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\")),\n            KeyValue::new(\"service.instance.id\", worker_id.to_string()),\n            KeyValue::new(\"needle.session_id\", session_id.to_string()),\n        ]);\n\n        // Add hostname from OS\n        if let Some(hostname) = gethostname::gethostname().to_str() {\n            builder = builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(\"host.name\", hostname.to_string())]);\n        }\n\n        // Add process PID\n        builder =\n            builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(\"process.pid\", std::process::id().to_string())]);\n\n        // Add computed needle.* attributes if provided\n        if let Some(agent_value) = agent {\n            builder =\n                builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(\"needle.agent\", agent_value.to_string())]);\n        }\n        if let Some(model_value) = model {\n            builder =\n                builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(\"needle.model\", model_value.to_string())]);\n        }\n        if let Some(provider_value) = provider {\n            builder = builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(\n                \"needle.model.provider\",\n                provider_value.to_string(),\n            )]);\n        }\n        if let Some(workspace_value) = workspace {\n            builder = builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(\n                \"needle.workspace\",\n                workspace_label(workspace_value),\n            )]);\n        }\n\n        // Add resource attributes from config (KEY=VALUE pairs)\n        // Validate that reserved keys are not being overridden\n        for attr_str in &config.resource_attributes {\n            if let Some((key, value)) = attr_str.split_once('=') {\n                if RESERVED_KEYS.contains(&key) {\n                    anyhow::bail!(\n                        \"cannot override reserved resource attribute '{key}' via config. \\\n                         Reserved keys are: service.name, service.instance.id\"\n                    );\n                }\n                builder =\n                    builder.with_attributes([KeyValue::new(key.to_string(), value.to_string())]);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // `Resource::builder()` has already applied the SDK detectors. Keep\n        // explicit NEEDLE attributes last so the SDK fallback\n        // `service.name=unknown_service` cannot overwrite `service.name`.\n        let resource = builder.build();\n\n        Ok(resource)\n    }\n\n    /// Build providers using gRPC transport (tonic).\n    pub fn build_grpc_providers(\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        resource: &Resource,\n        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,\n    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)> {\n        let metadata = Self::build_grpc_metadata(config)?;\n        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);\n\n        // Import the tonic-specific exporters\n        use opentelemetry_otlp::WithTonicConfig;\n        use opentelemetry_otlp::{LogExporter, SpanExporter, WithExportConfig};\n\n        // Build the transport exporters, then use the same provider path as the\n        // transport-seam tests below.\n        let base_span_exporter = SpanExporter::builder()\n            .with_tonic()\n            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())\n            .with_timeout(timeout)\n            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())\n            .build()?;\n        let base_log_exporter = LogExporter::builder()\n            .with_tonic()\n            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())\n            .with_timeout(timeout)\n            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())\n            .build()?;\n\n        Self::build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner(\n            config,\n            resource,\n            drop_tx,\n            metadata,\n            base_span_exporter,\n            base_log_exporter,\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Build gRPC providers with transport exporters supplied by the caller.\n    ///\n    /// This is the transport seam used by tests: the provider construction,\n    /// batch processors, resource assignment, and resilient wrappers are the\n    /// same path as [`Self::build_grpc_providers`], while the exporter at the\n    /// transport boundary can capture the resource it receives.\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn build_grpc_providers_with_exporters<S, L>(\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        resource: &Resource,\n        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,\n        span_exporter: S,\n        log_exporter: L,\n    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>\n    where\n        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,\n        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,\n    {\n        Self::build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner(\n            config,\n            resource,\n            drop_tx,\n            Self::build_grpc_metadata(config)?,\n            span_exporter,\n            log_exporter,\n        )\n    }\n\n    fn build_grpc_providers_with_exporters_inner<S, L>(\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        resource: &Resource,\n        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,\n        metadata: tonic::metadata::MetadataMap,\n        base_span_exporter: S,\n        base_log_exporter: L,\n    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>\n    where\n        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,\n        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,\n    {\n        use opentelemetry_otlp::{MetricExporter, WithExportConfig, WithTonicConfig};\n\n        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);\n\n        let span_exporter = ResilientGrpcSpanExporter::new(base_span_exporter, drop_tx.clone());\n        let batch_span_processor = BatchSpanProcessor::builder(span_exporter).build();\n        let tracer_provider = SdkTracerProvider::builder()\n            .with_span_processor(batch_span_processor)\n            .with_resource(resource.clone())\n            .build();\n\n        let metric_exporter = MetricExporter::builder()\n            .with_tonic()\n            .with_endpoint(config.endpoint.clone())\n            .with_timeout(timeout)\n            .with_metadata(metadata.clone())\n            .build()?;\n        let metric_reader = PeriodicReader::builder(metric_exporter)\n            .with_interval(Duration::from_secs(config.metrics_interval_secs))\n            .build();\n        let meter_provider = SdkMeterProvider::builder()\n            .with_reader(metric_reader)\n            .with_resource(resource.clone())\n            .build();\n\n        let log_exporter = ResilientGrpcLogExporter::new(base_log_exporter, drop_tx);\n        let batch_log_processor = BatchLogProcessor::builder(log_exporter).build();\n        let logger_provider = SdkLoggerProvider::builder()\n            .with_log_processor(batch_log_processor)\n            .with_resource(resource.clone())\n            .build();\n\n        Ok((tracer_provider, meter_provider, logger_provider))\n    }\n\n    fn build_grpc_metadata(config: &OtlpSinkConfig) -> Result<tonic::metadata::MetadataMap> {\n        use tonic::metadata::{MetadataKey, MetadataMap, MetadataValue};\n\n        let mut metadata = MetadataMap::new();\n        for (key, value) in resolve_headers(&config.headers)? {\n            let key_val = MetadataKey::from_bytes(key.as_bytes())\n                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!(\"invalid OTLP metadata header name '{key}'\"))?;\n            let metadata_value = MetadataValue::try_from(value.as_str())\n                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!(\"invalid value for OTLP metadata header '{key}'\"))?;\n            metadata.insert(key_val, metadata_value);\n        }\n        Ok(metadata)\n    }\n\n    /// Build providers using HTTP/protobuf transport (reqwest).\n    pub fn build_http_providers(\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        resource: &Resource,\n        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,\n    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)> {\n        use opentelemetry_otlp::WithHttpConfig;\n        use opentelemetry_otlp::{LogExporter, SpanExporter, WithExportConfig};\n\n        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);\n\n        let headers_map = Self::build_http_headers(config)?;\n\n        // opentelemetry-otlp only auto-appends the per-signal path\n        // (/v1/traces, /v1/metrics, /v1/logs) when the endpoint is resolved from\n        // an OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*_ENDPOINT env var. When `.with_endpoint()` is\n        // called programmatically (as we do here, from config.endpoint), the\n        // SDK uses it verbatim with no path appended - so without this, every\n        // HTTP export request hits the collector's bare root and gets a 404.\n        // Confirmed live 2026-08-12 (bf-6a617): reqwest::Error { kind: Status(404,\n        // None), url: \".../4318/\" }, and NEEDLE's own OTLP telemetry has never\n        // once reached the dashboard as a result.\n        let http_signal_endpoint =\n            |path: &str| format!(\"{}{}\", config.endpoint.trim_end_matches('/'), path);\n\n        // Build the transport exporters, then use the same provider path as the\n        // transport-seam tests below.\n        let base_span_exporter = SpanExporter::builder()\n            .with_http()\n            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint(\"/v1/traces\"))\n            .with_timeout(timeout)\n            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())\n            .build()?;\n        let base_log_exporter = LogExporter::builder()\n            .with_http()\n            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint(\"/v1/logs\"))\n            .with_timeout(timeout)\n            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())\n            .build()?;\n\n        Self::build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner(\n            config,\n            resource,\n            drop_tx,\n            headers_map,\n            base_span_exporter,\n            base_log_exporter,\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Build HTTP providers with transport exporters supplied by the caller.\n    ///\n    /// This is the transport seam used by tests: the provider construction,\n    /// batch processors, resource assignment, and resilient wrappers are the\n    /// same path as [`Self::build_http_providers`], while the exporter at the\n    /// transport boundary can capture the resource it receives.\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn build_http_providers_with_exporters<S, L>(\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        resource: &Resource,\n        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,\n        span_exporter: S,\n        log_exporter: L,\n    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>\n    where\n        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,\n        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,\n    {\n        Self::build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner(\n            config,\n            resource,\n            drop_tx,\n            Self::build_http_headers(config)?,\n            span_exporter,\n            log_exporter,\n        )\n    }\n\n    fn build_http_providers_with_exporters_inner<S, L>(\n        config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n        resource: &Resource,\n        drop_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<DropEvent>,\n        headers_map: HashMap<String, String>,\n        base_span_exporter: S,\n        base_log_exporter: L,\n    ) -> Result<(SdkTracerProvider, SdkMeterProvider, SdkLoggerProvider)>\n    where\n        S: SdkSpanExporter + 'static,\n        L: SdkLogExporter + 'static,\n    {\n        use opentelemetry_otlp::{MetricExporter, WithExportConfig, WithHttpConfig};\n\n        let timeout = Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms);\n        let http_signal_endpoint =\n            |path: &str| format!(\"{}{}\", config.endpoint.trim_end_matches('/'), path);\n\n        let span_exporter = ResilientHttpSpanExporter::new(base_span_exporter, drop_tx.clone());\n        let    .with_resource(resource.clone())\n            .build();\n\n        let metric_exporter = MetricExporter::builder()\n            .with_http()\n            .with_endpoint(http_signal_endpoint(\"/v1/metrics\"))\n            .with_timeout(timeout)\n            .with_headers(headers_map.clone())\n            .build()?;\n        let metric_reader = headers.into_iter().collect())\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch a telemetry event to the appropriate signal.\n    ///\n    /// Per the semantic mapping:\n    /// - Spans: bead.claim.attempted, lightweight\n    ///   consumers that do not query the trace backend\n    fn dispatch_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        // Keep a complete, self-contained event feed in the log backend. Traces\n        // and metrics remain the canonical analytical representations, while\n        // this log copy lets dashboards reconstruct worker state without\n        // joining three signal stores.\n        self.emit_log(event)?;\n\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            // Metrics: worker lifecycle\n            \"worker.started\" => {\n                self.metrics.workers_active.add(1, &[]);\n            }\n\n            \"worker.stopped\" => {\n                self.metrics.workers_active.add(-1, &[]);\n            }\n\n            // Events whose analytical representation is a span.\n            \"bead.claim.attempted\" => {\n                // Track claim attempts with result=\"attempting\"\n                self.metrics\n                    .claim_attempts\n                    .add(1, &[KeyValue::new(\"result\", \"attempting\")]);\n            }\n\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => {\n                // Track claim attempts with result=\"succeeded\"\n                self.metrics\n                    .claim_attempts\n                    .add(1, &[KeyValue::new(\"result\", \"succeeded\")]);\n\n                // Emit beads_claimed metric with strand and priority attributes\n                let strand = event\n                    .data\n                    .get(\"strand\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())\n                    .unwrap_or(0);\n                self.metrics.beads_claimed.add(\n                    1,\n                    &[\n                        KeyValue::new(\"strand\",      // Track claim attempts with result=\"race_lost\"\n                self.metrics\n                    .claim_attempts\n                    .add(1, &[KeyValue::new(\"result\", \"race_lost\")]);\n            }\n\n            \"bead.claim.failed\" => {\n                // Track claim attempts with result=\"failed\"\n                self.metrics\n                    .claim_attempts\n                    .add(1, &[KeyValue::new(\"result\", \"failed\")]);\n            }\n\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => {}\n\n            \"agent.completed\" => {\n                if let Some(duration_ms) = event.duration_ms {\n                    let exit_code = event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"exit_code\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())\n                        .unwrap_or(-1);\n\n                    // Extract agent and model from event data\n                    let agent = event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"agent\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n                    let model = event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"model\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n\n                    self.metrics.agent_duration.record(\n                        duration_ms as f64,\n                        &[\n                            KeyValue::new(\"agent\", agent.to_string()),\n                            KeyValue::new(\"model\", \"strand.evaluated\" => {\n                if let Some(duration_ms) = event.duration_ms {\n                    if let Some(strand_name) =\n                        event.data.get(\"strand_name\").and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    {\n                        let result = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"result\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                            .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n                        self.metrics.strand_duration.record(\n                            duration_ms as f64,\n                            &[\n                                KeyValue::new(\"strand\", strand_name.to_string()),\n                                KeyValue::new(\"result\", result.to_string()),\n                            ],\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            \"outcome.handled\" => {}\n\n            // Metrics: bead completion (also a span, but we need metrics)\n            \"bead.completed\" => {\n                if let Some(duration_ms) = event.duration_ms {\n                    let outcome = event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"outcome\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n                    self.metrics\n                        .beads_completed\n                        .add(1, &[KeyValue::new(\"outcome\", outcome.to_string())]);\n                    self.metrics.bead_duration.record(\n                        duration_ms as f64,\n                        &[KeyValue::new(\"outcome\", outcome.to_string())],\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Span events are also attached to the active span.\n            \"heartbeat.emitted\" | \"build.heartbeat\" => {\n                // Update heartbeat age observable state\n                let now = SystemTime::now()\n                    .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)\n                    .map(|d| d.as_secs())\n                    .unwrap_or(0);\n                self.observable_state\n                    .last_heartbeat_secs\n                    .store(now, Ordering::Relaxed);\n                self.emit_span_event(event)?;\n            }\n\n            // Metrics: effort.recorded (not a span, but metrics only)\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let agent = event\n                    .data\n                    .get(\"agent_name\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n                let model = event\n                    .data\n                    .get(\"model\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .unwrap_or(\"unknown\");\n                if let Some(tokens_in) = event.data.get(\"tokens_in\").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()) {\n                    self.metrics.tokens_input.add(\n                        tokens_in,\n                        &[\n                            KeyValue::new(\"agent\", agent.to_string()),\n                            KeyValue::new(\"model\", model.to_string()),\n                        ],\n                    );\n                }\n                if let Some(tokens_out) = event.data.get(\"tokens_out\").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()) {\n                    self.metrics.tokens_output.add(\n                        tokens_out,\n                        &[\n                            KeyValue::new(\"agent\", agent.to_string()),\n                            KeyValue::new(\"model\", model.to_string()),\n                        ],\n                    );\n                }\n                if let Some(cost) = event\n                    .data\n                    .get(\"estimated_cost_usd\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())\n                {\n \"peer.stale\" => {\n                self.metrics.peers_stale.add(1, &[]);\n            }\n\n            // Metrics: peer recovery (decrement stale count)\n            \"peer.crashed\" => {\n                self.metrics.peers_stale.add(-1, &[]);\n            }\n\n            // Metrics: mitosis child creation\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => {\n                if let Some(children_created)              // to maintain bounded cardinality. .add(children_created, &[]);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // All other events need no additional signal representation.\n            _ => {}\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Emit a telemetry event as a log record.\n    fn emit_log(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let logger = self.logger_provider.logger(\"needle\");\n\n        // Create log record and set its fields\n        let mut log_record = logger.create_log_record();\n\n        // Set severity\n        let severity = self.severity_for_event(&event.event_type);\n        log_record.set_severity_number(severity.0);\n        log_record.set_severity_text(severity.1);\n\n        // Set body\n        let body_str = serde_json::to_string(&event.data)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|_| \"{\\\"error\\\":\\\"failed to serialize data\\\"}\".to_string());\n        log_record.set_body(AnyValue::from(body_str));\n\n        // Set trace linkage using OTel LogRecord API (not as attributes)\n        // TraceId is 16 bytes (32 hex chars), SpanId is 8 bytes (16 hex chars)\n        if let (Some(ref trace_id), Some(ref span_id)) = (&event.trace_id, &event.span_id) {\n            if let (Ok(trace_bytes), Ok(span_bytes)) = (hex::decode(trace_id), hex::decode(span_id))\n            {\n                if let (Ok(trace_arr), Ok(span_arr)) = (\n                    trace_bytes.as_slice().try_into().map(|b: [u8; 16]| b),\n                    span_bytes.as_slice().try_into().map(|b: [u8; 8]| b),\n                ) {\n                    let trace_id = TraceId::from_bytes(trace_arr);\n                    let span_id = SpanId::from_bytes(span_arr);\n                    log_record.set_trace_context(trace_id, span_id, None);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Build and add attributes - explicit type to avoid inference errors\n        let mut attrs: Vec<(&str, AnyValue)> = Vec::with_capacity(9);\n        attrs.push((\"service.version\", AnyValue::from(env!(\"CARGO_PKG_VERSION\"))));\n        attrs.push((\"event_type\", event.event_type.clone().into()));\n        attrs.push((\"worker_id\", event.worker_id.clone().into()));\n        attrs.push((\"session_id\", event.session_id.clone().into()));\n        attrs.push((\"sequence\", AnyValue::from(event.sequence as i64)));\n\n        if let Some(ref bead_id) = event.bead_id {\n            attrs.push((\"bead_id\", bead_id.as_ref().to_string().into()));\n        }\n\n        if let Some(ref workspace) = event.workspace {\n            attrs.push((\n                \"workspace\",\n                workspace_label(&workspace.to_string_lossy()).into(),\n            ));\n        }\n\n        if let Some(duration_ms) = event.duration_ms {\n            attrs.push((\"duration_ms\", AnyValue::from(duration_ms as i64)));\n        }\n\n        // Add needle.agent, needle.model, and needle.model.provider from dispatch context when available.\n        // These per-record attributes reflect the actual adapter/model dispatched,\n        // which can differ from the configured default due to routing rules.\n        // Per ADR-016 §2: record value wins over Resource value.\n        if let Some(agent_name) = event.data.get(\"agent_name\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n            attrs.push((\"needle.agent\", agent_name.to_string().into()));\n        }\n        if let Some(model) = event.data.get(\"model\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n            attrs.push((\"needle.model\", model.to_string().into()));\n        }\n        if let Some(provider) = event.data.get(\"provider\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n            attrs.push((\"needle.model.provider\", provider.to_string().into()));\n        }\n\n        log_record.add_attributes(attrs);\n\n        logger.emit(log_record);\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Emit a telemetry event as a span event on the current span.\n    ///\n    /// Used for intra-span state changes like heartbeat.emitted and build.heartbeat.\n    fn emit_span_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        // Use tracing to emit a span event\n        // The event name is the event type, and the data is added as fields\n        let event_name = event.event_type.as_str();\n\n        // Build fields from event data\n        use std::borrow::Cow;\n        let mut fields = Vec::new();\n        fields.push((\"event_type\", Cow::Borrowed(event.event_type.as_str())));\n        fields.push((\"worker_id\", Cow::Borrowed(event.worker_id.as_str())));\n        fields.push((\"session_id\", Cow::Borrowed(event.session_id.as_str())));\n\n        if let Some(ref bead_id) = event.bead_id {\n            fields.push((\"bead_id\", Cow::Borrowed(&**bead_id)));\n        }\n\n        // Add any additional fields from the data JSON\n        if let Some(data_map) = event.data.as_object() {\n            for (key, value) in data_map {\n                if let Some(str_val) = value.as_str() {\n                    fields.push((key.as_str(), Cow::Borrowed(str_val)));\n                } else if let Some(num_val) = value.as_i64() {\n                    // Convert to owned string for numeric values\n                    fields.push((key.as_str(), Cow::Owned(num_val.to_string())));\n                } else if let Some(bool_val) = value.as_bool() {\n                    fields.push((\n                        key.as_str(),\n                        Cow::Borrowed(if bool_val { \"true\" } else { \"false\" }),\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Emit as a tracing event (which becomes an OTel span event)\n        tracing::event!(\n            tracing::Level::INFO,\n            name = event_name,\n            ?fields,\n            \"{}\",\n            event_name\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Map event type to OTel severity level.\n    fn severity_for_event(&self, event_type: &str) -> (Severity, &'static str) {\n        match event_type {\n            // ERROR events\n            \"worker.errored\"\n            | \"bead.claim.failed\"\n            | \"build.timeout\"           // agent timeout\n            | \"telemetry.otlp.dropped\"  // OTLP export drops\n            | \"telemetry.sink_error\"    // Sink errors (e.g., hook failures)\n            => (Severity::Error, \"ERROR\"),\n\n            // WARN events\n            \"peer.stale\"     // StuckDetected\n            | \"peer.crashed\" // StuckReleased\n            | \"fleet.cpu_saturated\" // System CPU load exceeds threshold\n            | \"fleet.memory_low\" // System memory below threshold\n            => (Severity::Warn, \"WARN\"),\n\n            // INFO events (default)\n            // Includes: worker.started, worker.stopped, health.check, effort.recorded,\n            //           bead.orphaned, bead.claim.race_lost, budget.warning, rate_limit.wait,\n            //           bead.released, transform.failed, worker.handling.timeout,\n            //           telemetry.otlp.shutdown_timeout, and everything else\n            _ => (Severity::Info, \"INFO\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Update the queue depth observable gauge.\n    ///\n    /// Called by strand evaluation to sample the current queue depth per priority.\n    /// This updates the per-priority counts that the observable gauge callback reads.\n    ///\n    /// The `depths` parameter maps priority level -> bead count at that priority.\n    pub fn record_queue_depth(&self, depths: HashMap<u8, u64>) {\n        let mut guard = self\n            .observable_state\n            .queue_depth_by_priority\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap();\n        for (priority, count) in depths {\n            guard\n                .entry(priority)\n                .or_insert_with(|| AtomicU64::new(0))\n                .store(count, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shutdown the OTLP sink, draining all batched exports.\n    ///\n    /// Has a hard 5-second deadline. If the shutdown takes longer than 5 seconds,\n    /// remaining batches are abandoned and a `telemetry.otlp.shutdown_timeout` event\n    /// is emitted to the file sink.\n    pub async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<()> {\n        const SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_SECS: u64 = 5;\n        let deadline = Duration::from_secs(SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_SECS);\n\n        // Shutdown in reverse order: logs, metrics, traces\n        // This ensures all dependent data is flushed first\n\n        // Use a timeout for each shutdown to enforce the deadline\n        // Split the deadline across all three providers\n        let per_provider_deadline = deadline.checked_div(3).unwrap_or(deadline);\n\n        let mut timed_out = false;\n\n        // Flush logger provider with timeout\n        let logger_provider = self.logger_provider.clone();\n        let logger_result = tokio::time::timeout(\n            per_provider_deadline,\n            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {\n                catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| logger_provider.shutdown()))\n            }),\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        match logger_result {\n            Ok(Ok(Ok(Ok(())))) => {}\n            Ok(Ok(Ok(Err(e)))) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP logger provider shutdown failed: {e}\");\n            }\n            Ok(Ok(Err(_))) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP logger provider shutdown panicked\");\n            }\n            Ok(Err(_)) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP logger provider spawn_blocking panicked\");\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP logger provider shutdown timed out after {per_provider_deadline:?}\");\n                timed_out = true;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Flush meter provider with timeout\n        let meter_provider = self.meter_provider.clone();\n        let meter_result = tokio::time::timeout(\n            per_provider_deadline,\n            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {\n                catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| meter_provider.shutdown()))\n            }),\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        match meter_result {\n            Ok(Ok(Ok(Ok(())))) => {}\n            Ok(Ok(Ok(Err(e)))) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP meter provider shutdown failed: {e}\");\n            }\n            Ok(Ok(Err(_))) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP meter provider shutdown panicked\");\n            }\n            Ok(Err(_)) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP meter provider spawn_blocking panicked\");\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP meter provider shutdown timed out after {per_provider_deadline:?}\");\n                timed_out = true;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Flush tracer provider with timeout\n        let tracer_provider = self.tracer_provider.clone();\n        let tracer_result = tokio::time::timeout(\n            per_provider_deadline,\n            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {\n                catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| tracer_provider.shutdown()))\n            }),\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        match tracer_result {\n            Ok(Ok(Ok(Ok(())))) => {}\n            Ok(Ok(Ok(Err(e)))) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP tracer provider shutdown failed: {e}\");\n            }\n            Ok(Ok(Err(_))) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP tracer provider shutdown panicked\");\n            }\n            Ok(Err(_)) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP tracer provider spawn_blocking panicked\");\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                warn!(\"OTLP tracer provider shutdown timed out after {per_provider_deadline:?}\");\n                timed_out = true;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // If any provider timed out, emit a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink\n        if timed_out {\n            if let Some(file_sink) = &self.file_sink {\n                let sequence = self.next_drop_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n                let timestamp = SystemTime::now();\n\n                let mut data = serde_json::map::Map::new();\n                data.insert(\n                    \"deadline_secs\".to_string(),\n                    serde_json::json!(SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_SECS),\n                );\n                data.insert(\"timed_out\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));\n\n                let event = TelemetryEvent {\n                    timestamp: chrono::DateTime::from(timestamp),\n                    event_type: \"telemetry.otlp.shutdown_timeout\".to_string(),\n                    worker_id: self.worker_id.clone(),\n                    session_id: self.session_id.clone(),\n                    sequence,\n                    bead_id: None,\n                    workspace: None,\n                    duration_ms: None,\n                    data: serde_json::Value::Object(data),\n                    trace_id: None,\n                    span_id: None,\n                };\n\n                let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n                    if let Err(e) = (**file_sink).accept(&event) {\n                        warn!(\"failed to write shutdown timeout event to file sink: {e}\");\n                    }\n                }));\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Create an OpenTelemetry tracing layer for the tracing subscriber.\n///\n/// This bridges `tracing` spans to the OTLP exporter, allowing use of\n/// `#[instrument]` macros throughout the codebase.\n///\n/// Returns `None` if the OTLP feature is not enabled or if the layer\n/// cannot be created.\n///\n/// The `agent`, `model`, and `workspace` parameters are optional resource\n/// attributes for OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.\n///\n/// Note: Drop events from the tracing layer are logged at WARN level\n/// rather than emitted to the file sink, because the tracing layer is\n/// created before the file sink is available.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\npub fn create_tracing_layer(\n    worker_id: String,\n    session_id: String,\n    config: &OtlpSinkConfig,\n    agent: Option<&str>,\n    model: Option<&str>,\n    workspace: Option<&str>,\n) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn tracing_subscriber::Layer<tracing_subscriber::Registry> + Send + Sync>>>\n{\n    if !config.enabled {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    // Build resource attributes from config + computed attributes\n    let resource = OtlpSink::build_resource(\n        &worker_id,\n        &session_id,\n        config,\n        agent,\n        model,\n        None,\n        workspace,\n    )?;\n\n    // Create drop channel for the tracing layer\n    // Dumps will be logged at WARN level rather than emitted as events\n    // Note: Drop handler spawn deferred to avoid runtime initialization issues\n    let (drop_tx, _drop_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<DropEvent>();\n\n    // Build exporters based on protocol\n    let (tracer_provider, ..) = match config.protocol.as_str() {\n        \"grpc\" => OtlpSink::build_grpc_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,\n        \"http\" | \"http/protobuf\" => OtlpSink::build_http_providers(config, &resource, drop_tx)?,\n        other => anyhow::bail!(\"invalid OTLP protocol: {other}, must be 'grpc' or 'http'\"),\n    };\n\n    // Create the tracing layer with the tracer provider, boxed for type erasure\n    let layer = tracing_opentelemetry::layer().with_tracer(tracer_provider.tracer(\"needle\"));\n    Ok(Some(Box::new(layer)))\n}\n\nimpl crate::telemetry::Sink for OtlpSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        // Wrap dispatch_event in catch_unwind to prevent OTel SDK panics\n        // from bubbling up to the worker loop. Log failures but don't propagate.\n        match catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| self.dispatch_event(event))) {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                // dispatch_event returned an error - log and suppress\n                warn!(\"OTLP sink dispatch error: {e}\");\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                // OTel SDK panicked - log and suppress\n                warn!(\"OTLP sink panicked while dispatching event\");\n                Ok(())\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        // Hard 5-second deadline for shutdown flush, per the OTLP resilience spec.\n        // This is a maximum time we're willing to wait for the collector to acknowledge\n        // all pending telemetry. Past this point, we abandon remaining batches and emit\n        // a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink.\n        let hard_deadline = Duration::from_secs(5).min(deadline);\n\n        // Clone Arcs for move into spawned threads\n        let tracer_provider = self.tracer_provider.clone();\n        let meter_provider = self.meter_provider.clone();\n        let logger_provider = self.logger_provider.clone();\n\n        // Spawn threads for each flush with timeout\n        let tracer_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n                tracer_provider.force_flush()\n            }))\n        });\n        let meter_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n                meter_provider.force_flush()\n            }))\n        });\n        let logger_handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {\n            catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n                logger_provider.force_flush()\n            }))\n        });\n\n        // Wait for each flush with the hard deadline\n        // Use join_timeout pattern: sleep for deadline, then check if thread is finished\n        let (tracer_result, tracer_timed_out) =\n            self.join_with_timeout(tracer_handle, hard_deadline, \"tracer\");\n        let (meter_result, meter_timed_out) =\n            self.join_with_timeout(meter_handle, hard_deadline, \"meter\");\n        let (logger_result, logger_timed_out) =\n            self.join_with_timeout(logger_handle, hard_deadline, \"logger\");\n\n        // Collect providers that timed out\n        let mut timed_out_providers = Vec::new();\n        if tracer_timed_out {\n            timed_out_providers.push(\"tracer\");\n        }\n        if meter_timed_out {\n            timed_out_providers.push(\"meter\");\n        }\n        if logger_timed_out {\n            timed_out_providers.push(\"logger\");\n        }\n\n        // Emit shutdown_timeout event if any provider timed out\n        if !timed_out_providers.is_empty() {\n            self.emit_shutdown_timeout_event(&timed_out_providers, hard_deadline);\n        }\n\n        // Check if any flush failed (but don't fail if they timed out - we already logged)\n        tracer_result.context(\"failed to flush tracer provider\")?;\n        meter_result.context(\"failed to flush meter provider\")?;\n        logger_result.context(\"failed to flush logger provider\")?;\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl OtlpSink {\n    /// Emit a shutdown_timeout event to the file sink.\n    ///\n    /// This event indicates that one or more OTLP providers failed to flush within\n    /// the 5-second shutdown deadline, causing remaining batches to be abandoned.\n    fn emit_shutdown_timeout_event(&self, providers: &[&str], deadline: Duration) {\n        if let Some(sink) = &self.file_sink {\n            let sequence = self.next_drop_sequence.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n\n            let mut data = serde_json::map::Map::new();\n            data.insert(\n                \"providers\".to_string(),\n                serde_json::json!(providers.join(\",\")),\n            );\n            data.insert(\n                \"deadline_secs\".to_string(),\n                serde_json::json!(deadline.as_secs_f64()),\n            );\n            data.insert(\"abandoned_batches\".to_string(), serde_json::json!(true));\n\n avoid recursion\n            let _ = catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {\n                if let Err(e) = (**sink).accept(&event) {\n                    warn!(\"failed to write OTLP shutdown_timeout event to file sink: {e}\");\n                }\n            }));\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Helper to join a thread with a timeout.\n    ///\n    /// This is a synchronous timeout implementation since we're not in an async context.\n    /// The pattern is: spawn thread, sleep for deadline, check if done.\n    /// If not done, we consider it timed out and return an error.\n    ///\n    /// Returns (result, timed_out) where timed_out is true if the thread did not\n    /// complete within the deadline.\n    fn join_with_timeout(\n        &self,\n        handle: std::thread::JoinHandle<\n            std::prelude::v1::Result<\n                std::prelude::v1::Result<(), opentelemetry_sdk::error::OTelSdkError>,\n                Box<dyn std::any::Any + Send>,\n            >,\n        >,\n        timeout: Duration,\n        name: &str,\n    ) -> (anyhow::Result<()>, bool) {\n        // Sleep for the timeout duration\n        std::thread::sleep(timeout);\n\n        // Check if the thread is done\n        if handle.is_finished() {\n            // Thread is done, join it (should return immediately)\n            match handle.join() {\n                Ok(Ok(result)) => {\n                    // Convert OTelSdkError to anyhow::Error\n                    (result.map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"{e}\")), false)\n                }\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    warn!(\"OTLP {name} provider flush failed: {:?}\", e);\n                    (Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\"{name} provider flush failed\")), false)\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    warn!(\"OTLP {name} provider flush panicked\");\n                    (Ok(()), false)\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Thread is still running, consider it timed out\n            warn!(\"OTLP {name} provider flush timed out after {timeout:?}\");\n            (Ok(()), true)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod Built-in defaults\n2. Global config file (`~/.config/needle/config.yaml`)\n3. Workspace config file (`.needle.yaml` in workspace root)\n4. Environment variables (`NEEDLE_*` prefix)\n5. CLI arguments\n\nThis guide covers the most commonly used configuration options.\n\n---\n\n## Worker Configuration\n\nThe `worker` section controls fleet behavior and worker spawning.\n\n### Basic Worker Settings\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworker:\n  max_workers: 4              # Maximum concurrent workers (default: 4)\n  idle_timeout: 60            # Seconds to wait between queue polls when idle (default: 60)\n  launch_stagger_seconds: 2   # Delay between worker launches (default: 2)\n```\n\n### Configuration Hot-Reload Check\n\n`worker.config_reload_check_interval_secs` controls how often a worker checks\nfor configuration changes at the cycle boundary, between dispatches. A value\nof `0` disables the check and is the default until the feature has had fleet\ntime:\n\n```yaml\nworker:\n  config_reload_check_interval_secs: 0  # Seconds between checks; 0 disables (default)\n```\n\nThis setting is Tier C (restart-required) because it gates the reload mechanism\nitself. In particular, a worker started with the default `0` cannot discover a\nfile change that enables polling; restart the worker after changing this value.\n\n### Worker Binary Path Override\n\n**When to use this:** Set `worker_binary_path` when the running binary's path is deliberately not what should be spawned as workers. This is needed in these cases:\n\n- **Wrapper script deployments:** If you run NEEDLE via a wrapper script (e.g., for environment setup or signal handling), the supervisor would spawn workers that re-execute the wrapper instead of the actual needle binary.\n- **PATH conflicts:** If another tool on your system is named `needle` and appears earlier in `$PATH`, workers would spawn the wrong binary without this override.\n- **Custom install locations:** If needle is installed at a non-standard path and you want to explicitly control which binary is spawned.\n\n**Default behavior:** When `worker_binary_path` is not set (or `null`), the supervisor resolves the worker binary via `std::env::current_exe()` — this is always correct when supervisor and workers are built from the same binary.\n\n**Example:**\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworker:\n  # Explicit path to the worker binary\n  # Use absolute paths or paths starting with ~ (expanded to $HOME)\n  worker_binary_path: /opt/needle/bin/needle\n\n  # Or use tilde expansion for home directory\n  # worker_binary_path: ~/local/bin/needle\n```\n\n**How it works:**\n\n- The supervisor logs the resolved binary path at startup (check your logs for \"worker spawn path resolved to...\")\n- The path is validated for existence at startup — a typo or missing binary will fail immediately, not silently spawn the wrong process\n- Relative paths are resolved relative to the supervisor's current working directory\n\n**Troubleshooting:**\n\n```bash\n# Check what binary your supervisor will spawn\nneedle supervise --dry-run\n\n# Verify the path exists and is executable\ntest -x /opt/needle/bin/needle && echo \"OK\" || echo \"MISSING\"\n\n# Check supervisor logs for the resolved path\ngrep \"worker spawn path\" ~/.needle/logs/supervisor.log\n```\n\n**See also:** GitHub issue [jedarden/NEEDLE#11](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/issues/11) — background on why this override exists.\n\n---\n\n## Agent Configuration\n\nThe `agent` section controls how NEEDLE invokes AI agents.\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nagent:\n  default: claude              # Default agent CLI (default: \"claude\")\n  timeout: 3600                # Agent process timeout in seconds (default: 3600 = 1 hour)\n  args: []                      # Extra arguments passed before the prompt (default: [])\n\n  # Directory containing adapter TOML files (default: ~/.config/needle/adapters)\n  adapters_dir: ~/.config/needle/adapters\n\n  # Model-to-adapter routing (optional)\n  routing:\n    # Rules are evaluated in order; first match wins\n    rules:\n      - match_model: \"(claude-)?(sonnet|opus|fable|haiku).*\"\n        adapter: claude-print    # Use subscription billing for Anthropic models\n    default_adapter: claude-code-glm-4.7  # Fallback for non-matching models\n    strict: false                # If true, fail when no rule matches (default: false)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Workspace Configuration\n\nThe `workspace` section defines where NEEDLE stores state and which workspace to process.\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworkspace:\n  # Default workspace directory (default: current directory)\n  default: ~/dev/my-project\n\n  # NEEDLE home directory for heartbeats and logs (default: ~/.needle)\n  home: ~/.needle\n\n  # Domain labels for cross-workspace skill sharing (optional)\n  labels:\n    - rust\n    - trading\n    - api\n```\n\n**Workspace overrides (`.needle.yaml`):**\n\nOnly certain fields can be overridden at the workspace level. Every workspace\nwith a bead store must explicitly bind its backend; NEEDLE does not infer store\nownership from whichever executable appears first on `PATH`.\n\n```yaml\n# .needle.yaml (in workspace root)\nworkspace:\n  labels:                    # ONLY this field is overridable at workspace level\n    - frontend\n    - react\n\nbead_cli:\n  backend: bead-forge       # Existing bead-forge workspace\n# backend: bead-rs          # Native bead-rs workspace after rehydration\n# explicit_path: /opt/bin/bead  # Optional host-specific operator override\n\n# These fields are ignored if set in .needle.yaml:\n# - workspace.default (resolved globally)\n# - workspace.home (resolved globally)\n```\n\n`bead-forge` resolves the `bf` executable and requires its identity to begin\nwith `bf `. `bead-rs` resolves `bead` and requires `bead `. Identity is checked\nbefore the store is opened. A missing, unknown, or mismatched binding makes the\nworkspace ineligible for dispatch. Changing this value does not migrate data:\ninitialize and reconcile the destination store first, then change the binding\nduring the reviewed cutover.\n\nExplore, Splice, and the supervisor load each target repository's binding\nindependently, so bead-forge and bead-rs workspaces can coexist during rollout.\n\n---\n\n## Strand Configuration\n\nNEEDLE runs multiple \"strands\" that find or create work when the primary workspace is empty.\n\n### Explore (Multi-workspace Discovery)\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nstrands:\n  explore:\n    enabled: true                          # Enable Explore strand (default: true)\n\n    # Leave empty for auto-discovery (recommended default)\n    # All directories under workspace_root containing .beads/ are scanned\n    workspaces: []\n\n    # Root for auto-discovery (default: $HOME)\n    workspace_root: ~/dev\n\n    # Minimum cycles between scans; empty scans back off geometrically (default: 1)\n    scan_interval_cycles: 1\n\n    # Maximum cycles between scans after backoff (default: 8)\n    max_scan_interval_cycles: 8\n\n    # Re-scan for new workspaces every N cycles (default: 60)\n    rediscovery_cycles: 60\n\n    # Alert if no beads claimed for this many minutes (default: 15)\n    starvation_threshold_minutes: 15\n```\n\n**Pinned mode (exception):** To restrict a worker to specific workspaces:\n\n```yaml\nstrands:\n  explore:\n    workspaces:\n      - ~/dev/project-a\n      - ~/dev/project-b\n    # WARNING: When workspaces is non-empty, auto-discovery is DISABLED\n    # and only the listed paths are scanned\n```\n\n### Mitosis (Bead Splitting)\n\n```yaml\nstrands:\n  mitosis:\n    enabled: true                # Enable mitosis (default: true)\n    first_failure_only: true     # Only split on first failure (default: true)\n    force_failure_threshold: 0  # Force split after N failures (0 = disabled)\n    repeat_interval: 0           # Re-split every N failures (0 = disabled)\n    max_depth: 0                # Maximum generation depth (0 = unlimited)\n\n    # Timeout-triggered mitosis (opt-in, default: disabled)\n    timeout_triggered:\n      enabled: false\n      agent_wallclock_timeout: false\n      handler_timeout: false\n      min_elapsed_fraction: 0.9  # Trigger only if 90% of timeout elapsed\n```\n\n### Weave, Unravel, Pulse (Opt-in Strands)\n\nThese strands are disabled by default — enable them explicitly:\n\n```yaml\nstrands:\n  weave:\n    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n    max_beads_per_run: 5       # Maximum beads to create per run\n    cooldown_hours: 24          # Minimum hours between runs\n    doc_patterns:\n      - \"README*\"\n      - \"AGENTS.md\"\n      - \"docs/**/*\"\n\n  unravel:\n    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n    max_beads_per_run: 5\n    max_alternatives_per_bead: 3\n    cooldown_hours: 168        # 7 days\n\n  pulse:\n    enabled: false              # Opt-in (default: false)\n    max_beads_per_run: 5\n    cooldown_hours: 48\n    severity_threshold: 3      # 1-5, where 1 is critical\n    scanners:\n      - name: clippy\n        command: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings\n```\n\n---\n\n## Telemetry Configuration\n\nNEEDLE emits structured telemetry (logs, metrics, traces) to multiple sinks.\n\n### File Sink (Local Logs)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  file_sink:\n    enabled: true               # Write logs to files (default: true)\n    log_dir: null               # Null = use workspace.home/logs\n    retention_days: 30          # Delete logs older than this (default: 30)\n```\n\n### Stdout Sink (Console Output)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  stdout_sink:\n    enabled: false               # Print to stdout (default: false)\n    format: normal               # minimal | normal | verbose (default: normal)\n    color: auto                 # auto | always | never (default: auto)\n```\n\n### OTLP Sink (OpenTelemetry Export)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  otlp_sink:\n    enabled: false               # Export to OTLP collector (default: false)\n    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC endpoint\n    protocol: \"grpc\"            # grpc | http\n    timeout_secs: 10            # Request timeout (default: 10)\n    compression: \"gzip\"          # gzip | none | zstd\n    tls:                        # Canonical TLS configuration\n      insecure: false           # Disable TLS verification (not recommended for production)\n      ca_file: \"\"               # Path to custom CA certificate (empty = system trust store)\n    headers: []                 # e.g. [\"Authorization: env:NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION\"]\n    resource_attributes: []     # Format: \"key=value\"\n    metrics_interval_secs: 10   # Metrics export interval (default: 10)\n    service_namespace: \"needle-fleet\"\n```\n\nThe mapping above is the canonical representation in v0.3.1 and later. For\nupgrade compatibility, legacy `tls: none` and `tls: tls` values are still\naccepted and normalize to `{insecure: true, ca_file: \"\"}` and\n`{insecure: false, ca_file: \"\"}` respectively. Convert those values to the\nmapping above when editing a config; unsupported values such as `mtls` produce\na validation error before the worker starts.\n\nIf the collector requires authorization, keep the secret out of YAML and use\nan environment reference in `headers`, for example\n`Authorization: env:NEEDLE_OTLP_AUTHORIZATION`. The environment variable must\ncontain the complete header value (such as `Bearer <token>`).\n\n### Webhooks (Hooks)\n\n```yaml\ntelemetry:\n  hooks:\n    - event_filter: \"outcome.*\"         # Glob pattern matched against event_type\n      command: \"/path/to/alert.sh\"      # Shell command (event JSON via stdin)\n      url: \"https://hooks.slack.com/...\"  # Webhook URL (optional)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Health Configuration\n\n```yaml\nhealth:\n  # Heartbeat interval in seconds (default: 30)\n  heartbeat_interval_secs: 30\n\n  # Heartbeat TTL in seconds (default: 300)\n  # Heartbeats older than this are considered stale\n  heartbeat_ttl_secs: 300\n\n  # Directory for heartbeat files (default: state/heartbeats under workspace.home)\n  heartbeat_dir: null\n```\n\n---\n\n## Validation Configuration\n\n```yaml\nvalidation:\n  # Timeout for gate execution in seconds (default: 50)\n  outcome_timeout_seconds: 50\n\n  # Maximum bytes of gate command stderr captured on failure (default: 4096)\n  stderr_cap_bytes: 4096\n```\n\n---\n\n## Supervisor Configuration\n\n```yaml\nsupervisor:\n  # Path to supervisor's heartbeat file\n  # (default: workspace.home/state/supervisor-heartbeat.json)\n  heartbeat_path: null\n\n  # Path to supervisor's control socket (optional)\n  socket_path: null\n```\n\n---\n\n## Environment Variable Overrides\n\nAny config field can be overridden via environment variables with the `NEEDLE_` prefix and `__` as separator:\n\n```bash\n# Set agent default\nexport NEEDLE_AGENT__DEFAULT=claude-interactive\n\n# Set timeout\nexport NEEDLE_AGENT__TIMEOUT=7200\n\n# Set routing\nexport NEEDLE_AGENT__ROUTING__DEFAULT_ADAPTER=claude-print\n\n# Set worker limits\nexport NEEDLE_WORKER__MAX_WORKERS=8\nexport NEEDLE_WORKER__IDLE_TIMEOUT=120\n\n# Set workspace\nexport NEEDLE_WORKSPACE__DEFAULT=~/dev/my-project\n```\n\n---\n\n## Complete Example Configuration\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/needle/config.yaml\nworker:\n  max_workers: 4\n  idle_timeout: 60\n  launch_stagger_seconds: 2\n  worker_binary_path: /opt/needle/bin/needle  #
